sanskrit: upasṛtya tadā droṇam uccair idam abhāṣata yasyārthe śastram ādhatse yam avekṣya ca jīvasi putras te dayito nityaṃ śo 'śvatthāmā nipātitaḥ
english: Then he drew near to Droṇa and spoke aloud these words: "He for whose sake you take up your weapon, he by looking on whom you go on living, your beloved son Aśvatthāman has been struck down."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vimanās tatra ācāryo mahad apriyam niyamya divyāny astrāṇi nāyudhyata yathā purā
english: Hearing that grievous news, the teacher there grew sick at heart, and withholding his celestial weapons he fought no longer as he had before.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramodvignaṃ śokopahatacetasam pāñcālarājasya sutaḥ krūrakarmā samādravat
english: Seeing him utterly stricken, his mind overwhelmed by grief, the son of the Pāñcāla king, a doer of cruel deeds, rushed upon him.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vihitaṃ mṛtyuṃ lokatattvavicakṣaṇaḥ divyāny astrāṇy athotsṛjya raṇe prāya upāviśat
english: Seeing that his death was ordained, he, skilled in the true nature of the worlds, then cast aside his celestial weapons and sat down upon the field, fasting unto death.

sanskrit: tato 'sya keśān savyena gṛhītvā pāṇinā tadā pārṣataḥ krośamānānāṃ vīrāṇām acchinac chiraḥ
english: Then the son of Pṛṣata, seizing his hair with his left hand, severed his head while the heroes cried out in protest.

sanskrit: na hantavyo na hantavya iti te sarvato 'bruvan tathaiva cārjuno vāhād avaruhyainam ādravat
english: "He must not be slain, he must not be slain!" they cried out on every side, and Arjuna too, leaping down from his chariot, ran toward him.

sanskrit: udyamya bāhū tvarito bruvāṇaś ca punaḥ punaḥ jīvantam ānayācāryaṃ mā vadhīr iti dharmavit
english: Raising his arms in haste and crying again and again, that knower of righteousness called out, "Bring the teacher to me alive—do not kill him!"

sanskrit: tathāpi vāryamāṇena kauravair arjunena ca hata eva nṛśaṃsena pitā tava nararṣabha
english: Yet even so, though forbidden by the Kauravas and by Arjuna, your father was slain outright by that ruthless one, O bull among men.

sanskrit: sainikāś ca tataḥ sarve prādravanta bhayārditāḥ vayaṃ cāpi nirutsāhā hate pitari te 'nagha
english: Then all the soldiers fled, tormented by fear, and we too were robbed of spirit, O blameless one, when your father had been slain.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tac chrutvā droṇaputras tu nidhanaṃ pitur āhave krodham āhārayat tīvraṃ padāhata ivoragaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: But when the son of Droṇa heard of his father's death in battle, he gathered a fierce wrath, like a serpent trodden underfoot.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca adharmeṇa hataṃ śrutvā dhṛṣṭadyumnena saṃjaya brāhmaṇaṃ pitaraṃ vṛddham aśvatthāmā kim abravīt
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When he heard, Saṃjaya, that his aged father, the brāhmaṇa, had been slain unrighteously by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, what did Aśvatthāman say?

sanskrit: mānuṣaṃ vāruṇāgneyaṃ brāhmam astraṃ ca vīryavān aindraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ caiva yasmin nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: He, the mighty one, in whom were ever established the human weapon, those of Varuṇa and Agni, the weapon of Brahmā, that of Indra, and the Nārāyaṇa weapon as well—

sanskrit: tam adharmeṇa dharmiṣṭhaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnena saṃjaya śrutvā nihatam ācāryam aśvatthāmā kim abravīt
english: When he heard, Saṃjaya, that the teacher, most righteous of men, had been slain unrighteously by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, what did Aśvatthāman say?

sanskrit: yena rāmād avāpyeha dhanurvedaṃ mahātmanā proktāny astrāṇi divyāni putrāya gurukāṅkṣiṇe
english: He, the great soul, who having gained the science of archery from Rāma, declared its celestial weapons to his son who longed for his teacher's lore—

sanskrit: ekam eva hi loke 'sminn ātmano guṇavattaram icchanti putraṃ puruṣā loke nānyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: For in this world men desire one thing alone—a son more excellent than themselves; none other, in any way, in all the world.

sanskrit: ācāryāṇāṃ bhavanty eva rahasyāni mahātmanām tāni putrāya vā dadyuḥ śiṣyāyānugatāya vā
english: Great-souled teachers do indeed have their secret lore, and this they would impart either to a son or to a devoted disciple.

sanskrit: sa śilpaṃ prāpya tat sarvaṃ saviśeṣaṃ ca saṃjaya śūraḥ śāradvatīputraḥ saṃkhye droṇād anantaraḥ
english: Having received all that craft, and with special favor besides, Saṃjaya, the valiant son of Śāradvatī's lord stood second only to Droṇa in battle.

sanskrit: rāmasyānumataḥ śāstre puraṃdarasamo yudhi kārtavīryasamo vīrye bṛhaspatisamo matau
english: Approved by Rāma in the science of arms, the equal of Purandara in battle, of Kārtavīrya in valor, of Bṛhaspati in wisdom,

sanskrit: mahīdharasamo dhṛtyā tejasāgnisamo yuvā samudra iva gāmbhīrye krodhe sarpaviṣopamaḥ
english: the equal of a mountain in steadfastness, of Agni in splendor, that youth—deep as the ocean in gravity, and in his wrath like the venom of a serpent.

sanskrit: sa rathī prathamo loke dṛḍhadhanvā jitaklamaḥ śīghro 'nila ivākrande caran kruddha ivāntakaḥ
english: He, the foremost chariot-warrior in the world, of unyielding bow, conqueror of fatigue, swift as the wind upon the field of clamor, ranging like Death enraged—

sanskrit: asyatā yena saṃgrāme dharaṇyabhinipīḍitā yo na vyathati saṃgrāme vīraḥ satyaparākramaḥ
english: by whose shooting the earth was pressed down hard in battle, that hero of unfailing prowess who never falters in the fight—

sanskrit: vedasnāto vratasnāto dhanurvede ca pāragaḥ mahodadhir ivākṣobhyo rāmo dāśarathir yathā
english: bathed in the Vedas, bathed in vows, and master to the end of the science of archery, unshakable as the great ocean, like Rāma the son of Daśaratha.

sanskrit: tam adharmeṇa dharmiṣṭhaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnena saṃyuge śrutvā nihatam ācāryam aśvatthāmā kim abravīt
english: When he heard that the teacher, most righteous of men, had been slain unrighteously by Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the encounter, what did Aśvatthāman say?

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnasya yo mṛtyuḥ sṛṣṭas tena mahātmanā yathā droṇasya pāñcālyo yajñasenasuto 'bhavat
english: As the Pāñcāla prince, the son of Yajñasena, was made the death ordained for Droṇa by that great soul, so was a death likewise ordained for Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: taṃ nṛśaṃsena pāpena krūreṇātyalpadarśinā śrutvā nihatam ācāryam aśvatthāmā kim abravīt
english: When he heard that the teacher had been slain by that ruthless, wicked, cruel man of meanest vision, what did Aśvatthāman say?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca chadmanā nihataṃ śrutvā pitaraṃ pāpakarmaṇā bāṣpeṇāpūryata drauṇī roṣeṇa ca nararṣabha
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing that his father had been slain by treachery by that doer of evil deeds, the son of Droṇa was filled with tears and with fury, O bull among men.

sanskrit: tasya kruddhasya rājendra vapur divyam adṛśyata antakasyeva bhūtāni jihīrṣoḥ kālaparyaye
english: As he raged, O lord of kings, his form appeared more than mortal, like that of Death itself, eager to take away all beings at the turning of the age.

sanskrit: aśrupūrṇe tato netre apamṛjya punaḥ punaḥ uvāca kopān niḥśvasya duryodhanam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then, wiping again and again his eyes that brimmed with tears, sighing in his anger, he spoke these words to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: pitā mama yathā kṣudrair nyastaśastro nipātitaḥ dharmadhvajavatā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tad viditaṃ mama anāryaṃ sunṛśaṃsasya dharmaputrasya me śrutam
english: "How my father, having laid down his weapons, was struck down by base men—I know that this sin was wrought by one who flaunts the banner of righteousness; ignoble it was, and I have heard of it from that most ruthless son of Dharma."

sanskrit: yuddheṣv api pravṛttānāṃ dhruvau jayaparājayau dvayam etad bhaved rājan vadhas tatra praśasyate
english: "For those engaged in battles, victory and defeat are both certain; either of the two may come to pass, O king, and slaying therein is held praiseworthy."

sanskrit: nyāyavṛtto vadho yas tu saṃgrāme yudhyato bhavet na sa duḥkhāya bhavati tathā dṛṣṭo hi sa dvijaḥ
english: "But a slaying that befalls a man fighting in battle by lawful conduct brings no cause for grief; in such wise was that twice-born one seen to fall."

sanskrit: gataḥ sa vīralokāya pitā mama na saṃśayaḥ na śocyaḥ puruṣavyāghras tathā sa nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: "My father has gone to the world of heroes, of that there is no doubt; nor is that tiger among men to be mourned, having met his end in such a way."

sanskrit: yat tu dharmapravṛttaḥ san keśagrahaṇam āptavān paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ tan me marmāṇi kṛntati
english: "But that he, engaged in righteousness, should suffer his hair to be seized in the sight of all the armies—that cuts through my very vitals."

sanskrit: kāmāt krodhād avajñānād darpād bālyena vā punaḥ vaidharmikāni kurvanti tathā paribhavena ca
english: "Out of desire, out of wrath, out of contempt, out of pride, or again out of childishness, and out of insolence too, men do deeds contrary to righteousness."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ pārṣateneha mahad ādharmikaṃ kṛtam avajñāya ca māṃ nūnaṃ nṛśaṃsena durātmanā
english: "This great unrighteous deed has been done here by the son of Pṛṣata—surely in contempt of me, by that ruthless and evil-souled wretch."

sanskrit: tasyānubandhaṃ sa draṣṭā dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ sudāruṇam anāryaṃ paramaṃ kṛtvā mithyāvādī ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "That Dhṛṣṭadyumna shall behold the dire consequence of it, having wrought a most ignoble deed; and the lying Pāṇḍava too shall behold it."

sanskrit: yo hy asau chadmanācāryaṃ śastraṃ saṃnyāsayat tadā tasyādya dharmarājasya bhūmiḥ pāsyati śoṇitam
english: "He who by treachery made the teacher lay down his weapon then—the earth shall today drink the blood of that king of righteousness."

sanskrit: sarvopāyair yatiṣyāmi pāñcālānām ahaṃ vadhe dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca samare hantāhaṃ pāpakāriṇam
english: "By every means I shall strive for the destruction of the Pāñcālas, and in battle I shall slay that doer of evil, Dhṛṣṭadyumna."

sanskrit: karmaṇā yena teneha mṛdunā dāruṇena vā pāñcālānāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā śāntiṃ labdhāsmi kaurava
english: "By whatever deed it be—gentle or terrible—having wrought the slaughter of the Pāñcālas, I shall win peace, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ puruṣavyāghra putram icchanti mānavāḥ pretya ceha ca saṃprāptaṃ trāṇāya mahato bhayāt
english: "That for which men desire a son, O tiger among men—deliverance both hereafter and here from great fear—that has now come to be."

sanskrit: pitrā tu mama sāvasthā prāptā nirbandhunā yathā mayi śailapratīkāśe putre śiṣye ca jīvati
english: "Yet my father came to such a plight, as though he had no kinsman at all, while I, his son and disciple, mountain-like, was living still."

sanskrit: dhiṅ mamāstrāṇi divyāni dhig bāhū dhik parākramam yan māṃ droṇaḥ sutaṃ prāpya keśagrahaṇam āptavān
english: "A curse upon my celestial weapons, a curse upon my arms, a curse upon my prowess—that Droṇa, though he had me for a son, should suffer his hair to be seized!"

sanskrit: sa tathāhaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā bharatasattama paralokagatasyāpi gamiṣyāmy anṛṇaḥ pituḥ
english: "So shall I act, O best of the Bharatas, that even toward my father gone to the other world I shall pass free of all debt to him."

sanskrit: āryeṇa tu na vaktavyā kadā cit stutir ātmanaḥ pitur vadham amṛṣyaṃs tu vakṣyāmy adyeha pauruṣam
english: "A noble man should never speak praise of himself; yet, unable to bear my father's slaying, I shall today proclaim my manhood here."

sanskrit: adya paśyantu me vīryaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ sajanārdanāḥ mṛdnataḥ sarvasainyāni yugāntam iva kurvataḥ
english: "Let the Pāṇḍavas with Janārdana behold my valor today, as I crush all their armies, working as it were the end of the age."

sanskrit: na hi devā na gandharvā nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ adya śaktā raṇe jetuṃ rathasthaṃ māṃ nararṣabha
english: "For neither gods nor gandharvas, neither asuras nor rākṣasas are able today to conquer me in battle, mounted on my chariot, O bull among men."

sanskrit: mad anyo nāsti loke 'sminn arjunād vāstravittamaḥ ahaṃ hi jvalatāṃ madhye mayūkhānām ivāṃśumān prayoktā devasṛṣṭānām astrāṇāṃ pṛtanāgataḥ
english: "There is none in this world, save Arjuna, who knows weapons better than I; for I, come into the host, am a wielder of the weapons fashioned by the gods, blazing like the sun among its rays."

sanskrit: kṛśāśvatanayā hy adya matprayuktā mahāmṛdhe darśayanto ''tmano vīryaṃ pramathiṣyanti pāṇḍavān
english: "For today the offspring of Kṛśāśva, loosed by me in the great fray, displaying their own might, shall crush the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: adya sarvā diśo rājan dhārābhir iva saṃkulāḥ āvṛtāḥ patribhis tīkṣṇair draṣṭāro māmakair iha
english: "Today, O king, men shall behold all the quarters thronged, as it were with torrents, covered over with my keen feathered shafts."

sanskrit: kiran hi śarajālāni sarvato bhairavasvaram śatrūn nipātayiṣyāmi mahāvāta iva drumān
english: "Scattering nets of arrows on every side with a fearful roar, I shall lay the enemy low, as a great wind lays low the trees."

sanskrit: na ca jānāti bībhatsus tad astraṃ na janārdanaḥ na bhīmaseno na yamau na ca rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "Neither Bībhatsu knows that weapon, nor Janārdana, nor Bhīmasena, nor the twins, nor King Yudhiṣṭhira;"

sanskrit: na pārṣato durātmāsau na śikhaṇḍī na sātyakiḥ yad idaṃ mayi kauravya sakalyaṃ sanivartanam
english: "nor that evil-souled son of Pṛṣata, nor Śikhaṇḍin, nor Sātyaki—this art, complete with its means of recall, that lies in me, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: nārāyaṇāya me pitrā praṇamya vidhipūrvakam upahāraḥ purā datto brahmarūpa upasthite
english: "Long ago my father, bowing down to Nārāyaṇa with due rite, offered an oblation when the god appeared in the form of Brahmā."

sanskrit: taṃ svayaṃ pratigṛhyātha bhagavān sa varaṃ dadau vavre pitā me paramam astraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tataḥ
english: "Then the Blessed One, accepting it in person, granted a boon; and my father thereupon chose the supreme weapon, the Nārāyaṇa."

sanskrit: athainam abravīd rājan bhagavān devasattamaḥ bhavitā tvatsamo nānyaḥ kaś cid yudhi naraḥ kva cit
english: "Then, O king, the Blessed One, best of the gods, said to him: 'There shall be no other man anywhere, ever, equal to you in battle.'"

sanskrit: na tv idaṃ sahasā brahman prayoktavyaṃ kathaṃ cana na hy etad astram anyatra vadhāc chatror nivartate
english: "'But this, O brāhmaṇa, is in no way to be loosed rashly; for this weapon turns not back save by the slaying of the foe.'"

sanskrit: na caitac chakyate jñātuṃ ko na vadhyed iti prabho avadhyam api hanyād dhi tasmān naitat prayojayet
english: "'And it cannot be known, O lord, who shall not be slain by it; indeed it would strike down even one who ought not to be slain—therefore one should not employ it lightly.'"

sanskrit: vadhaḥ saṃkhye dravaś caiva śastrāṇāṃ ca visarjanam prayācanaṃ ca śatrūṇāṃ gamanaṃ śaraṇasya ca
english: "Slaughter in battle, or flight, or the laying down of weapons, or the foes' suing for mercy, or the seeking of refuge—"

sanskrit: ete praśamane yogā mahāstrasya paraṃtapa sarvathā pīḍito hi syād avadhyān pīḍayan raṇe
english: "these are the means of quelling the great weapon, O scorcher of foes; for in every way he who, harassing in battle, harms those who ought not to be slain, would himself be afflicted."

sanskrit: taj jagrāha pitā mahyam abravīc caiva sa prabhuḥ tvaṃ varṣiṣyasi divyāni śastravarṣāṇy anekaśaḥ anenāstreṇa saṃgrāme tejasā ca jvaliṣyasi
english: "My father received it, and the Lord said to him: 'You shall pour down celestial showers of weapons again and again; with this weapon in battle you shall blaze forth in splendor.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa bhagavān divam ācakrame prabhuḥ etan nārāyaṇād astraṃ tat prāptaṃ mama bandhunā
english: "Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord ascended to heaven; this is the weapon gained from Nārāyaṇa by my kinsman."

sanskrit: tenāhaṃ pāṇḍavāṃś caiva pāñcālān matsyakekayān vidrāvayiṣyāmi raṇe śacīpatir ivāsurān
english: "With it I shall scatter in battle the Pāṇḍavas, the Pāñcālas, the Matsyas and the Kekayas, as the lord of Śacī scatters the asuras."

sanskrit: yathā yathāham iccheyaṃ tathā bhūtvā śarā mama nipateyuḥ sapatneṣu vikramatsv api bhārata
english: "In whatever fashion I may wish, in just that fashion my arrows, becoming so, shall fall upon my foes even as they show their prowess, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: yatheṣṭam aśmavarṣeṇa pravarṣiṣye raṇe sthitaḥ ayomukhaiś ca vihagair drāvayiṣye mahārathān paraśvadhāṃś ca vividhān prasakṣye 'ham asaṃśayam
english: "Standing in the field, I shall rain down at will a shower of stones, and with iron-beaked birds I shall drive off the great chariot-warriors, and I shall hurl forth manifold battle-axes—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ nārāyaṇāstreṇa mahatā śatrutāpana śatrūn vidhvaṃsayiṣyāmi kadarthīkṛtya pāṇḍavān
english: "With the mighty Nārāyaṇa weapon, O scorcher of foes, I shall shatter the enemy and bring the Pāṇḍavas to naught."

sanskrit: mitrabrahmagurudveṣī jālmakaḥ suvigarhitaḥ pāñcālāpasadaś cādya na me jīvan vimokṣyate
english: "That hater of friends, of brāhmaṇas, and of teachers, that base and utterly contemptible outcast of the Pāñcālas shall not escape me alive today."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā droṇaputrasya paryavartata vāhinī tataḥ sarve mahāśaṅkhān dadhmuḥ puruṣasattamāḥ
english: Hearing that, the host of the son of Droṇa rallied and turned back, and then all those best of men blew their great conches.

sanskrit: bherīś cābhyahanan hṛṣṭā ḍiṇḍimāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ tathā nanāda vasudhā khuranemiprapīḍitā sa śabdas tumulaḥ khaṃ dyāṃ pṛthivīṃ ca vyanādayat
english: In their joy they beat their kettledrums and tabors by the thousand; the earth too resounded, pressed by hooves and wheel-rims, and that tumultuous din made sky, heaven, and earth ring out.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdaṃ pāṇḍavāḥ śrutvā parjanyaninadopamam sametya rathināṃ śreṣṭhāḥ sahitāḥ saṃnyamantrayan
english: Hearing that sound, like the roar of a thundercloud, the Pāṇḍavas, those foremost of chariot-warriors, came together and took counsel as one.

sanskrit: tathoktvā droṇaputro 'pi tadopaspṛśya bhārata prāduścakāra tad divyam astraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tadā
english: And having spoken thus, the son of Droṇa too, having sipped water in due rite, then brought forth that celestial weapon, the Nārāyaṇa, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prādurbhūte tatas tasminn astre nārāyaṇe tadā prāvāt sapṛṣato vāyur anabhre stanayitnumān
english: Saṃjaya said: When that Nārāyaṇa weapon had then appeared, a wind blew laden with raindrops, and thunder rolled in a cloudless sky.

sanskrit: cacāla pṛthivī cāpi cukṣubhe ca mahodadhiḥ pratisrotaḥ pravṛttāś ca gantuṃ tatra samudragāḥ
english: The earth too quaked, and the great ocean was stirred, and the rivers that flow to the sea began to run there against their current.

sanskrit: śikharāṇi vyadīryanta girīṇāṃ tatra bhārata apasavyaṃ mṛgāś caiva pāṇḍuputrān pracakrire
english: The peaks of the mountains split asunder there, O Bhārata, and the beasts kept the sons of Pāṇḍu on their left as an ill omen.

sanskrit: tamasā cāvakīryanta sūryaś ca kaluṣo 'bhavat saṃpatanti ca bhūtāni kravyādāni prahṛṣṭavat
english: All things were strewn over with darkness, and the sun grew dim; and the flesh-eating creatures came flocking together as though delighted.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvās trastā āsan viśāṃ pate kathaṃ kathābhavat tīvrā dṛṣṭvā tad vyākulaṃ mahat
english: Gods, dānavas, and gandharvas were filled with terror, O lord of peoples, and a sharp dismay arose—"What is this? What is this?"—as they beheld that great turmoil.

sanskrit: vyathitāḥ sarvarājānas tadā hy āsan vicetasaḥ tad dṛṣṭvā ghorarūpaṃ tu drauṇer astraṃ bhayāvaham
english: All the kings then grew distressed and bewildered, beholding the dreadful, terror-bringing weapon of the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca nivartiteṣu sainyeṣu droṇaputreṇa saṃyuge bhṛśaṃ śokābhitaptena pitur vadham amṛṣyatā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the armies had been turned back in the encounter by the son of Droṇa, sorely scorched by grief and unable to bear his father's slaying,

sanskrit: kurūn āpatato dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya rakṣaṇe ko mantraḥ pāṇḍaveṣv āsīt tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: and when the Pāṇḍavas saw the Kurus bearing down upon them, what counsel was there among them for the protection of Dhṛṣṭadyumna? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prāg eva vidrutān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān yudhiṣṭhiraḥ punaś ca tumulaṃ śabdaṃ śrutvārjunam abhāṣata
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who had fled before, and hearing once again the tumultuous din, Yudhiṣṭhira spoke to Arjuna:

sanskrit: ācārye nihate droṇe dhṛṣṭadyumnena saṃyuge nihate vajrahastena yathā vṛtre mahāsure
english: "Now that the teacher Droṇa has been slain by Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the encounter, even as the great asura Vṛtra was slain by the wielder of the thunderbolt—"
